question.problem:
Find the sum modulo $25$ of the solutions to the congruence $10x≡15\,(\text{mod}\,25).$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
question.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=10$ and $n=25$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(10,25)=5.
$$

Since $b=15$ is divisible by $5,$ our congruence has $5$ solutions.

First, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}10x & ≡15 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ 5\cdot 2x & ≡5\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5\cdot 5) \\ \cancel{5}\cdot 2x & ≡\cancel{5}\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{5}\cdot 5) \\ 2x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=2$ and ${n}_{1}=5$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(2,5)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $5.$

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $2\,(\text{mod}\,5).$ To find the inverse of $2\,(\text{mod}\,5),$ we compute the exponents of $2\,(\text{mod}\,5)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ {2}^{3} & ≡4\cdot 2≡8≡5+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ {2}^{4} & ≡3\cdot 2≡6≡5+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $2\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5),$ which means that $3$ is the multiplicative inverse of $2$ (modulo $5$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $3,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ 3\cdot 2x & ≡3\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ (3\cdot 2)x & ≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x & ≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x & ≡5+4 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,5).$ 

But our original congruence was modulo $25$ (not modulo $5$). To find all the solutions modulo $25,$ we repeatedly add $5$ modulo $25$ until we reach the number $4$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡4+5≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡9+5≡14 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡14+5≡19 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡19+5≡24 &  & (\text{mod}\,25) \\ {x}_{6} & ≡24+5≡29≡25+4≡4≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,25)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x≡4,9,14,19,24\,(\text{mod}\,25).$ 

Finally,

$$
4+9+14+19+24≡70≡2\cdot 25+20≡20\,(\text{mod}\,25).
$$
